3

This document describes the architecture, the shared modules, the build and the tests of the Portable Web App Suite. For end-user instructions see the . Planning documents (feasibility study, decision log, spike results) are in docs/planning/ (English only).

Principles

  • One file per application: every application is a single HTML file with all code, styles, libraries and WebAssembly modules. It runs from file:// without a server and without an internet connection.
  • No node/npm: the sources are plain JavaScript. A Python script (build.py, standard library only) bundles them. Third-party libraries are vendored in vendor/.
  • No secrets in browser storage: all file:// pages share one storage area (Chromium and Firefox), so application data (connections, credentials) is kept in user files (JSON or KeePass). Browser storage only holds preferences (language, theme, app settings, spelling language and personal words), recently used file handles, recovery copies of unsaved work (never of an unlocked KeePass database) and dictionaries loaded by the user.
  • Offline by default: a Content Security Policy in every page forbids network connections, unless the application has network functions.
  • Inputs and re-renders: Preact sets value on every render when it differs from the DOM. Inputs that commit only on change, blur or Enter (renaming, tags, names) therefore use defaultValue (with a key that changes with the model value), otherwise a re-render in between (a timer, a hover) would replace half-typed text.

Build

bash

build.py replaces in src/index.html:

Source Result
<link rel="stylesheet" href> inline <style>
<script src> / <script type="module" src> inline script
<script type="importmap" data-src="a.json b.json"> ES modules as text; a small script creates Blob URLs and the import map before any module runs
<script type="application/octet-stream" id data-src> binary file, gzip + base64 (shared/js/embed.js unpacks it)
<script type="application/octet-stream" data-bundle="bundle.json"> all files of a bundle (used for Pyodide and for the apps in the overview, which is built last)
<script type="text/plain" id data-src> text, e.g. worker code
</head> (every page) #suite-about (copyright, licence, source URL, version, the line of MODIFIED) and #suite-licenses (see Licences)

The build is reproducible: the same sources give a byte-identical file.

Licences

Before inlining, build.py inserts two elements into every page. #suite-about (JSON) is read at once by the shell: the about dialog shows copyright, licence and source URL, and when the first line of the file MODIFIED (or of $SUITE_MODIFIED_FILE) is present, the dialog starts with "Modified version: …", the header shows a badge and the window title ends with "(modified version)" – the visible notice that NOTICE.md asks of modified versions. #suite-licenses (gzip + base64 JSON, decoded with DecompressionStream when the licence section is opened) holds the EUPL in English and German, the two halves of NOTICE.md and the third-party components of the page with their licence texts (deduplicated by hash): the packages of the vendor/esm/*/lock.json files that the page's import maps use, the Python packages of vendor/pyodide/licenses.json (texts read from the wheels) and the entries of vendor/components.json whose path prefix the page references (classic builds, engines, fonts, code bundled in other packages; extends adds texts to a lock-file component); missing texts come from vendor/licenses/spdx/. The overview lists the components of all apps it embeds. Tests: tests/apps/test_licence.py (licence, notice and components with texts in English and German, only the components of an app, the marks of a build with MODIFIED).

Embedded modules get blob: URLs, against which relative specifiers cannot be resolved. An application's own modules therefore import each other with bare specifiers (@app/doc.js) that the application's js/importmap.json maps to the files; this works the same in the source tree and in the built file.

Hosted PWA variant

python3 tools/build_pwa.py [dir] (default build/pwa, git-ignored) turns the built apps into a web site that can be installed: each <app>.html gets a <link rel="manifest">, the registration of sw.js (only on http/https) and a CSP extended by manifest-src 'self' and 'self' in worker-src/img-src; next to it <app>.webmanifest (id/start URL ./<app>.html, standalone, the favicon as icons/<app>.svg, file_handlers with the extensions of the app from the app list in shared/js/bridge.js) and index.html forwarding to the overview. The service worker uses one cache: the overview, manifests and icons are added on installation, every other file on its first load; requests are answered from the cache and refreshed in the background (stale-while-revalidate, query strings ignored). Files opened through a file handler arrive at window.launchQueue; Suite.bridge.receive passes the first one with its real FileSystemFileHandle to the app (so saving writes back). Serve .webmanifest as application/manifest+json. Test: tests/apps/test_pwa.py (output, offline reload and the forwarding index in Chromium, the launch queue with a stub).

Releases and the public repository

A release sets VERSION (shown in the about dialogs), rebuilds dist/ and the documentation, writes dist/SHA256SUMS (checksums of the built apps, so that users can check that they run an unmodified build) and is tagged v<version>. python3 tools/publish_release.py v<version> [directory] then mirrors the tag into the public repository (default ../portable-web-app-suite-public): one commit and one annotated tag per release, as "Adrian Fuchs github@adrianfuchs.at", with the tracked files of the tag (git archive) but without dist/ (the built apps and SHA256SUMS are attached to the GitHub release instead). The development history is not published. Before committing, the tool refuses files with private information: e-mail addresses other than example domains and the public address (outside vendor/), private keys, access tokens, local home paths.

Platform restrictions of file://

  • External module scripts are blocked; modules are therefore embedded and loaded from Blob URLs.
  • Workers cannot load ES modules (no module workers from Blob URLs in Chromium, no import() or importScripts() of Blob URLs in workers). Worker code is one classic script.
  • No SharedArrayBuffer (no cross-origin isolation): only single-threaded WebAssembly.
  • File System Access API only in Chromium on the desktop; elsewhere files are downloaded.

Vendored libraries

  • Classic browser builds are downloaded with curl (see vendor/README.md).
  • ES-module packages are vendored with tools/vendor_esm.py <manifest> from jsDelivr's +esm endpoint: one version per package, imports rewritten to bare specifiers, license texts and versions recorded, optional stub modules for excluded lazily loaded modules.
  • Pyodide and Python packages: tools/vendor_pyodide.py vendor/pyodide.json (SHA-256 checked).
  • The SSH/SFTP engine: tools/build_engine_ssh.py (needs Go; the result is committed).

Spell checking

shared/js/spell.js wraps hunspell-asm (Hunspell compiled to WebAssembly; the apps' CSP allows 'wasm-unsafe-eval' and connect-src data:). Dictionaries are converted to UTF-8 before Hunspell reads them (decoded in the character set of the SET line, SET UTF-8 written), so words go in and come out as JavaScript strings for every dictionary. The service spell holds the suite-wide setting (suite.spell.enabled, suite.spell.language – default from the UI language), the built-in dictionaries (embedded as #dict-en_US-aff/-dic, #dict-de_DE-aff/-dic, gzip, read with Suite.embed.bytes only when checking starts), user dictionaries (IndexedDB suite-dictionaries; .aff+.dic pairs or the dictionaries/ of an .oxt, without hyph_/th_ files), personal words (suite.spell.words, added to every checker) and ignored words (session); words() drops chunks with digits, _, @, /, ://, single letters and all-caps words; onChange informs the views, also about changes in other tabs (storage event).

shared/js/spell-dom.js (imported by the eleven apps with prose; calendar and KeePass load it as a module script) adds the selector to the header (Suite.shell.addHeaderItem) and marks unknown words with one CSS Custom Highlight (suite-spell): in contenteditable elements on their text nodes (not in code, pre, links); for <textarea> and <input data-spell> on a mirror – a fixed, transparent copy of the field with the same box, font and scroll position in a layer above the page, shown only while a point of the field is the top-most element (elementFromPoint), so that dialogs and drawers covering it hide its marks. Fields with spellcheck="false" (code, addresses), read-only and non-text inputs and CodeMirror editors are left out; in checked fields the browser's checking is switched off (spellcheck="false", restored when spelling is off). Updates run in requestAnimationFrame after input, scrolling, resizing and DOM mutations. The context menu (contextmenu in the capture phase, not with Shift) finds the word at the caret (fields) or at caretPositionFromPoint/caretRangeFromPoint (contenteditable) and replaces through execCommand('insertText'), which keeps the undo history and fires input. shared/js/cm-spell.js is the CodeMirror counterpart: a view plugin builds mark decorations (cm-spell-error) for the visible ranges – in "prose" mode everything except Markdown code, URLs and HTML, in "code" mode only syntax nodes named *Comment*, *String*, *Docstring* – and handles the context menu; the text editor chooses the mode from the document's language, the notebook from the cell type. The document editor keeps its panel (canvas). Tests: tests/apps/test_spelling.py (German compounds and suggestions in the text editor, personal words, code mode, textarea mirror and contenteditable in mail with menu, ignore and Shift, the setting shared between apps, an .oxt in ISO-8859-1 from the header, the menu on a phone), spelling cells in test_notebook.py, the panel in test_document.py.

Undo and redo

Every editor has undo/redo with toolbar buttons (data-testid undo/redo, needed on touch devices) and the shortcuts of Suite.UndoHistory.key. Text fields keep the browser's own undo. Strategies:

Application Undo
Text editor, SQL/body editors, notebook cell text CodeMirror history per document/editor (@codemirror/commands undo/redo)
Spreadsheet, document Univer's command history (toolbar buttons of Univer)
Archive manager snapshots of the entry list (entries copied shallowly; their load() closures keep the data)
KeePass Database.snapshot()/restore() in kdbx.js: deep copy of the group tree with kdbxweb's copyFrom (protected values stay encrypted in memory), deleted objects and metadata; a snapshot is taken after every change and the previous one goes to the history; locking clears it
Calendar snapshots of the events, name, color and VCALENDAR of all open calendars (opening/closing files is not a step)
Notebook cell list snapshots referring to the cell objects (editors are kept); outputs are only restored for clearing outputs and type changes
Database tool SQLite: exported database file before every change (driver.restore()), up to 20 steps and 32 MiB; Postgres: inverse statements for grid edits
HTTP analyzer snapshots of the collection after every change; typing in one field (by input event target) within a second is merged
Hex, image, diagram, presentation, audio, video editors own snapshot histories (see the sections of the applications)

App bridge (“Open with…”)

shared/js/bridge.js passes a file from a source app to a target app and saves it back:

  1. The source calls Suite.bridge.openWith(name, { data, save, source, exclude }) from a click. The chooser lists the apps registered for the extension (APPS; the hex editor opens anything).
  2. Standalone: the source opens new URL('<app>.html', location.href) with window.open (synchronously, for popup blockers). The target calls Suite.bridge.receive(onOpen) at start and posts { suite: 'suite-bridge', type: 'ready' } to its opener; the source answers with { type: 'open', name, fileType, bytes, writable, source } and, for writable files, transfers one end of a MessageChannel. In the overview (window name suite-hub-app), the source sends { type: 'open-in', app, … } to the overview instead, which opens a tab and forwards file and port when the tab is ready.
  3. The target gets { file, handle }. The handle (bridged: true) implements getFile, queryPermission, requestPermission and createWritable; Suite.files.save() writes through it, which sends { type: 'save', id, bytes } over the port. The source's save(bytes) callback writes the data back (archive entry, SFTP/FTP upload, KeePass attachment, Pyodide file) and answers saved or error. Read-only copies (received mail attachments) have no handle, so saving downloads.

Sources: archive manager, FTP/SFTP client, SSH file panel, KeePass attachments, mail attachments, notebook files, the overview. Targets: every app that opens files.

Application data format

JSON:

js

KeePass: group Portable Web App Suite/<app>. The settings are the attachment settings.json of the entry Settings. Every connection is an entry with the custom field SuiteId; name, username, password, url and notes are stored in the standard fields, other properties as custom fields (text as it is, other values as JSON); password, privateKey, passphrase, token, secret and apiKey are protected.

The app suite holds what all apps share: settings.relay and settings.preferences, the localStorage entries of the suite (keys suite.* and <app>.prefs, without suite.mediaplayer.resume) as strings. Suite.preferences (end of shared/js/shell.js) collects and applies them; the about dialog exports them as a JSON file in this format (suite-settings.json, only apps.suite.settings.preferences) and imports the same part of any JSON app data file, then asks to reload. Suite.appdata writes the current preferences into every connection file it saves and, when a file with different preferences is opened, shows a banner to apply them. Test: tests/apps/test_preferences.py.

Applications

Text editor (apps/texteditor)

File Content
js/encoding.js TE.encoding: detection (BOM, valid UTF-8, UTF-16 without BOM by zero bytes, else Windows-1252) and encoding of UTF-8 (± BOM), UTF-16 LE/BE (± BOM), Windows-1252; line endings LF/CRLF/CR. The editor works with \n internally and converts when saving.
js/languages.js Module app/languages: language by file name/extension, CodeMirror language support (lang-* packages and legacy modes).
split view A second EditorView with its own state on the same document: both views get a custom dispatch that forwards document changes to the other one, marked with an Annotation so they are not echoed back (with the original user event, so the main view's history groups them). Only the main view keeps the history; the second view maps undo/redo to it.
find in files runFind() searches the EditorState documents of all tabs, or – with a FileSystemDirectoryHandle from showDirectoryPicker – the files of a folder (async generator, debounced input, a newer search cancels an older one); matches keep their document offsets so that a click selects them.
@codemirror/merge Comparing: MergeView (two editors; the left one read-only, revertControls: "a-to-b") or, below 760 px, unifiedMergeView in one editor; getChunks counts the differences, goToNextChunk/goToPreviousChunk navigate. The result replaces the document in one transaction when the comparison ends.
js/tools.js Module app/tools: text tools as pure string functions (apply(id, text)); line tools sort with Intl.Collator (numeric, base sensitivity, stable), XML is re-indented from a DOMParser tree. main.js applies a tool to the selection (extended to whole lines for line tools) or the document as one transaction (userEvent: input.tool).
js/main.js One CodeMirror EditorView; every tab keeps its own EditorState (undo history, selection), swapped with setState. Settings (wrap, whitespace, font size, dark theme) are compartments that are reconfigured when switching tabs. Toolbar, tabs and status bar are Preact components in the shared shell.

Multiple cursors use CodeMirror's built-in support (allowMultipleSelections, Ctrl+click, rectangular selection with Alt+drag, selectNextOccurrence). A document counts as changed if its text differs from the last saved text (Text.eq). View preferences are stored in localStorage (texteditor.prefs); file contents never are.

Tests: tests/apps/test_texteditor.py (languages, encoding round trips, conversion, tabs, search/replace, go to line, multiple cursors, preferences, German interface, phone layout, write-back with the File System Access API, text tools on the document and the selection, encoders/formatters, invalid input, comparing with an open document and a file, split view (changes both ways, shared undo, following the tab), find in open files (case, regular expressions, errors) and in a folder (OPFS directory standing in for the picker; .git and binary files skipped)).

Hex editor (apps/hexeditor)

File Content
js/buffer.js HE.ByteBuffer: bytes in a growable Uint8Array with the operations replace, insert and remove; every operation returns its inverse, which gives undo/redo (the two nibbles of a typed byte are one undo step). find() searches forwards/backwards, HE.parseHex() parses hexadecimal input, HE.inspect() interprets bytes for the data inspector (DataView, BigInt).
js/checksum.js HE.checksums(): CRC-32 and Adler-32 (tables/loops), MD5 (RFC 1321, WebCrypto has none) and SHA-1/256/512 via crypto.subtle.digest; HE.differences() counts differing bytes of two arrays.
js/main.js UI in the shared shell: virtualized view (only visible rows plus a margin are rendered into an absolutely positioned spacer; row height 22 px), keyboard and pointer handling, search bar, go-to bar, inspector, status bar, checksum dialog, comparison (second column rendered per visible row, so scrolling is shared; the difference count is recomputed when the buffer version changes, next/previous difference scans from the cursor).

The whole file is kept in memory; files above 256 MiB trigger a warning. Bytes per row default to 8 (narrow screens), 16 or 32 (wide screens). Preferences (bytes per row, byte order) are stored in localStorage (hexeditor.prefs).

Tests: tests/apps/test_hexeditor.py (overwrite, ASCII input, appending, insert, delete, undo/redo, search, go to, inspector, saving, 16 MiB file, mouse selection and copy, German interface, phone editing via the inspector, write-back, checksums against Python's hashlib/zlib incl. MD5 padding edge cases, comparison with navigation and recount after editing).

PDF viewer (apps/pdfviewer)

Signatures (js/signatures.js, no libraries): findSignatures scans the raw bytes for /ByteRange [0 a b c]; /Contents is the hex string in the gap between the two ranges, the other keys (/Name, /M, /Reason, /Location, /SubFilter) are read from the dictionary text around it. A small DER reader parses the CMS SignedData: the signer certificate (issuer + serial or the first one), the digest algorithm, the signed attributes (messageDigest, signingTime) and the signature. Integrity = SHA digest of both ranges equals messageDigest; signature = crypto.subtle.verify over the signed attributes re-tagged as SET (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, RSA-PSS with the hash and salt from its parameters, ECDSA with the DER signature converted to r‖s; RSA keys are re-wrapped as rsaEncryption SPKI). Bytes after the last range mean changes after signing. The certificate chain inside the signature is verified link by link; trust is not decided (no root store offline).

PDF.js (pdfjs-dist, Apache-2.0) is vendored with tools/vendor_pdfjs.py <version> into vendor/pdfjs/:

File Use
pdf.min.mjs, pdf_viewer.mjs ES modules (import map pdfjs-dist, pdfjs-dist/web/pdf_viewer); the viewer components read the library from globalThis.pdfjsLib, so main.js sets it before importing them
pdf.worker.classic.js the worker converted to a classic script (export removed, import.meta.url replaced) and started from a Blob URL (GlobalWorkerOptions.workerPort)
pdf_viewer.css viewer styles with the referenced images inlined as data: URLs
cmaps/, standard_fonts/, wasm/ embedded with data-bundle; an own BinaryDataFactory (useWorkerFetch: false) serves them from the bundle instead of fetching URLs

getDocument runs with isEvalSupported: false (no eval under the CSP) and useSystemFonts: false (the system font path would load the standard fonts by URL). The PDFViewer container is created once outside Preact and attached to the layout (it must be absolutely positioned and survive re-renders). Thumbnails are rendered lazily with an IntersectionObserver. Saving uses saveDocument() when form data or annotations exist, otherwise getData(). Printing renders every page into an image in #pv-print and calls window.print(); a print style sheet hides the app.

Page operations (js/pages.js) use pdf-lib 1.17 (MIT, vendor/esm/pdflib, imported on first use). Each operation loads the current bytes (with form data and annotations, saveDocument()), changes the document in place (setRotation, removePage, insertPage of the existing page objects for reordering, copyPages from other files), saves it and reopens the result in the viewer at the affected page; the previous bytes go onto an undo stack (30 steps). Extracting copies pages into a new document. pdf-lib cannot write encrypted files; such PDFs report an error. Signing is a page operation too: the signature pad (a 600×200 canvas, pointer strokes or typed text in a script font) is cropped to its ink and saved as PNG; the click position on the page canvas is converted with the page view's viewport.convertToPdfPoint() and pages.stamp() draws the image there (embedPng, drawImage, 180 pt wide at most).

Tests: tests/apps/test_pdfviewer.py with PDFs written by tests/helpers/office_samples.make_pdf() (Helvetica text that is not embedded, outline, internal link, form field; encrypted with pypdf): rendering, text layer, thumbnails, navigation, outline, links, zoom, rotation, search, form filling and ink annotations checked with pypdf, password, printing, page operations (move, rotate, delete and undo, append, extract; order, rotation and form checked with pypdf), protected PDFs, German interface, phone layout, signing (drawn signature as an image XObject, empty pad, cancelled placement).

KeePass (apps/keepass)

The application works directly on the Suite.kdbx database object (kdbxweb); vendor/otpauth.umd.min.js (otpauth, MIT) computes TOTP codes from an otp field (otpauth:// URI, KeePassXC convention). js/generator.js provides KP.generatePassword(options) (rejection sampling with crypto.getRandomValues, at least one character of each selected class) and KP.entropy(password) (character pool estimate).

  • Editing: setFields(entry, values, { history }) pushes the previous state into the entry history only on the first change of an editing session (state.historyPushed), not on every key press. Protected custom fields are ProtectedValues.
  • Deleting entries and groups moves them into the recycle bin (created on demand, meta.recycleBinUuid); groups() and entries() of Suite.kdbx skip the bin, the UI looks up the selected group including the bin.
  • Saving goes through db.save() (re-opens the result to verify it) and Suite.files.save/saveAs; a new database is saved with “save as”. Key files are created with kdbxweb.Credentials.createRandomKeyFile(2) (XML key file v2, .keyx).
  • Auto-lock after 15 minutes without pointer/keyboard activity, skipped while there are unsaved changes; the clipboard is cleared 30 seconds after copying.
  • Layout: three panes (groups, entries, editor); below 760 px only one pane (pane-groups|entries|entry) is visible.

Tests: tests/apps/test_keepass.py creates databases with pykeepass and checks every saved file with pykeepass: wrong password, browsing, search, TOTP code, editing with history, custom and protected fields, tags, groups, moving, history restore, recycle bin, new database with key file, master key change, generator, attachments, lock and auto-lock (Playwright clock), merging a copy (synchronized with kdbxweb's merge, which requires the same root group UUID) and another database (imported with importEntry into a new group), password report, German interface, phone layout.

Archive manager (apps/archive)

js/archive.js (ES module, fflate for deflate/gzip) parses and writes the container formats itself; js/multi.js reads the other formats and writes 7z through libarchive.js 2.0 (libarchive as WebAssembly, vendor/libarchive, tools/vendor_libarchive.py):

  • The worker bundle (classic script after replacing import.meta.url; module workers from Blob URLs do not start in file:// pages) and the wasm are embedded by build.py. The worker has its own opaque origin and cannot fetch the page's Blob URLs, so the wasm is patched into it as a data: URL. Two more patches: a larger output buffer for writing (libarchive.js reserves only 128 bytes per file, too little for headers) and printErr as warning. Archive.init({ getWorker }) starts it.
  • detectMulti recognises the formats by magic numbers; readMulti extracts all entries at once (client.extractFiles(), libarchive reads sequentially) and keeps them in memory. libarchive decrypts no 7z/RAR: encrypted ones give ar.encryptedUnsupported; no entries from xz/bzip2/zstd/lzma data means a single compressed file (raw format not enabled).

  • write7z: libarchive.js has no working "no filter" option, so the 7z stream is written through the gzip filter and unpacked with DecompressionStream. Entries carry no folder records (folders come from the paths) and no encryption.

  • ZIP reading starts at the end-of-central-directory record (ZIP64 locator and extra field supported). Entries are listed from the central directory without decompressing; load() inflates on demand and checks the CRC-32. Names are UTF-8 (flag 11 or valid UTF-8) or CP437; the Info-ZIP Unicode path (0x7075), extended timestamp (0x5455) and Unix modes are read.

  • ZIP writing sets the UTF-8 flag and an extended timestamp. Unchanged entries of the opened archive are copied with their compressed data (entry.zip.raw()); encrypted entries keep their flags, extra fields and data descriptor. New or changed entries are deflated with the chosen level (stored when that is not smaller). No ZIP64 writing: more than 4 GiB or 65,535 entries is an error.
  • TAR reads ustar headers with prefix, pax (path, linkpath, mtime), GNU long names (L/K) and base-256 sizes, and writes ustar plus pax headers for long or non-ASCII names. GZ keeps the original file name (FNAME).
  • 7z, RAR, bzip2 and xz are detected by their signature and reported as unsupported.
  • Encryption (js/zipcrypto.js, synchronous so that load() stays synchronous): SHA-1, HMAC-SHA1, PBKDF2 and the AES block cipher (T-tables; checked against the FIPS-197 and RFC 6070 test vectors) are implemented in the module, because WebCrypto is asynchronous and its AES-CTR counts big-endian while WinZip AES uses Gladman's little-endian counter. WinZip AES (method 99, extra field 0x9901): PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with 1000 iterations derives key, HMAC key and the 2-byte verifier from password (UTF-8) and salt; data = salt + verifier + AES-CTR data + 10 bytes HMAC-SHA1; AE-2 (no CRC) is written with AES-256. ZipCrypto: the 12th header byte checks the password against the CRC (or the DOS time with flag 3). archive.js keeps the entered passwords (addPassword), locked(entry) checks them cheaply with the verifier, and write(..., { encryption: { password, method, all } }) encrypts new and changed (with all also unchanged unencrypted) entries; encrypted unchanged entries are copied raw.

js/main.js keeps a flat entry list; folders implied by paths are shown without an entry of their own. Adding content creates explicit folder entries for its parents. After saving, the written bytes are read again so that the state matches the file. Extracting several items uses showDirectoryPicker() where available, otherwise one ZIP download. Folder drops are read with webkitGetAsEntry(). main.js imports @app/archive.js (see Build).

Tests: tests/apps/test_archive.py creates archives with zipfile, tarfile and gzip (and a ZipCrypto archive written by the test) and checks every saved file with them: browsing, preview, sorting, adding, folders, renaming, deleting, raw copy of unchanged entries, compression level, TAR.GZ long/Unicode names and symbolic links, conversion to TAR and ZIP, GZ, ZipCrypto password prompt and encryption of added files (checked with zipfile), AES archives from pyzipper read and written as AES-256 and ZipCrypto (checked with pyzipper and zipfile), extraction (download, ZIP, folder via OPFS), integrity test (intact archive, stored entry with a changed byte), unsupported formats, drag and drop, German interface, phone layout.

Media player (apps/mediaplayer)

One <video> element (created once outside Preact and attached to the stage) plays audio and video from Blob URLs of the selected files or from stream URLs; the CSP allows media-src blob: data: http: https:. No decoder is bundled: the formats are those of the browser.

  • js/tags.js reads tags from the first 512 KiB (ID3v2.2–2.4 incl. APIC, FLAC Vorbis comments and PICTURE, Ogg Vorbis/Opus comments, RIFF INFO and id3 chunks, MP4 ilst) and ID3v1 from the end of the file.
  • js/playlist.js parses M3U/M3U8 (#EXTINF), PLS and XSPF, writes M3U8 and converts SRT to WebVTT (subtitles are attached as <track> with a Blob URL).
  • Playlist entries are matched with the added files by file name (case-insensitive); missing entries wait for a file with that name. .m3u files have the MIME type audio/x-mpegurl and are therefore excluded from the media files explicitly.
  • Durations are probed one after another with a hidden <audio preload=metadata>.
  • Shuffle keeps a random order with the current item first; with repeat “all” a new order is drawn at the end.
  • Media Session metadata and action handlers; preferences (volume, mute, speed, shuffle, repeat, playlist visibility) in localStorage (suite.mediaplayer).

Equaliser: a second media element is created on first use and routed through createMediaElementSource → ten BiquadFilterNodes (low shelf, eight peaking filters with Q 1.4, high shelf) → optionally a DynamicsCompressor (threshold −24 dB, ratio 4) with make-up gain → destination. Local files play through this element while the equaliser is on; stream URLs always use the plain element, because routing media without CORS headers through Web Audio silences it. useElement() swaps the elements (keeping volume, speed and position). A–B repeat checks the position every animation frame; frame steps move by 1/30 s; snapshots draw the video into a canvas. Resume positions (files of two minutes or more, name and size as key) are kept in localStorage (suite.mediaplayer.resume, 200 entries).

Tests: tests/apps/test_mediaplayer.py with WAV files written by tests/helpers/media_samples.py (RIFF INFO and ID3 tags, cover) and a WebM video made with ffmpeg (skipped without ffmpeg): tags, durations, playback, automatic advance, repeat modes, keyboard, preferences, playlist import (M3U, PLS, XSPF) and export, missing entries, subtitles, video, unplayable files, shuffle, reordering, filter, URLs, equaliser (element switch during playback, filter gains, preferences), A–B repeat, resume position, album view, frame steps and snapshot size, German interface, phone layout.

Image editor (apps/imageeditor)

ES modules: doc.js (document model and file formats, imports fflate), tools.js, filters.js, guides.js (rulers, snapping), main.js (UI).

  • Document: every layer is a canvas of the image size with visible, opacity and blend (canvas composite operations); compositing draws the layers in order. The selection is a rectangle or ellipse used as clip path; selectionMask() gives an alpha mask for pixel operations (fill, convolution, auto levels).
  • History: before a change the affected state is captured (layer: a copy of one layer, props: layer properties, coalesced while a slider is dragged, doc: all layers and the size). Undo captures the current state into the redo stack and restores the snapshot. The history is limited to 50 steps and 512 MiB.
  • View: one canvas (outside Preact) sized to the stage in device pixels; zoom and pan are a transform. Painting draws into a stroke canvas that is composed with the layer copy into ed.preview (uniform opacity within a stroke, eraser as destination-out, clipped to the selection); the preview replaces the layer while drawing and becomes the layer at the end. Coalesced pointer events and pen pressure are used; two touch pointers switch to pinch zoom.
  • Retouching (tools.js): the clone stamp, healing brush and blur/sharpen brush paint soft round dabs (a cached radial-alpha mask, every size/4 pixels along the stroke) of a source image into the stroke canvas: the layer copy at the clone offset, or a blurred copy (ctx.filter = blur()) / an unsharp-masked copy (x + (x − blur(x))). Healing replaces the clone at the end of the stroke by clone + blur(layer) − blur(clone) inside the painted area (healArea), so the texture comes from the source and the low frequencies (colour, brightness) from the destination. Smudge works on a copy of the layer that is updated dab by dab: each dab copies the pixels of the previous position with the opacity as strength.
  • Rulers, guides, grid: the stage is a grid of two ruler canvases and the canvas box (built outside Preact). Guides (ed.guides, { axis: 'h' | 'v', pos }) lie on pixel boundaries; dragging from a ruler uses pointer capture on the ruler. guides.js snapPoint snaps to guides, image edges and the nearest grid lines within snapDistance / zoom; tools with snaps: true get snapped coordinates (marked snappedX/Y), which the selection tools treat as pixel boundaries instead of including the pixel under the pointer. The move tool snaps the moved selection's edges (snapRect). Preferences are stored in localStorage (suite.imageeditor.view).
  • Filters: CSS filters via ctx.filter (live preview while the dialog is open), 3×3 convolution and auto levels on ImageData. Selections are rect, ellipse, poly (lasso; points relative to x/y) or mask (magic wand and every combined selection: runs of pixels [dx, dy, length, …] relative to x/y), so moving a selection only changes x and y and selectionPath can clip with all of them. Combining (add, subtract, intersect, invert) works on selectionMask() and turns the result back into runs (maskSelection); the marching ants of a mask follow its pixel border (selectionOutline, cached per selection). The magic wand shares the region search of the fill tool (regionMask). Levels and curves build 256-entry lookup tables (levels: outBlack + (outWhite − outBlack) · x^(1/γ); curves: monotone cubic Hermite interpolation after Fritsch–Carlson, so the curve never overshoots); the RGB table is applied first, then the channel's own (channelLuts). The preview is the layer with the tables applied, shown through ed.preview and recomputed once per frame; these dialogs (and the adjustments) do not dim the image.
  • Files: decoding through <img>/Blob URL; encoding with canvas.toBlob (PNG, JPEG, WebP), an own 24-bit BMP writer and OpenRaster (mimetype stored first, stack.xml top layer first, data/*.png, mergedimage.png, thumbnail). PSD with ag-psd (vendor/esm/psd, MIT, with pako; imported on first use): layers are read bottom-up with their offsets, groups flattened (hidden/opacity inherited), layer masks multiplied into the alpha (defaultColor outside the mask rectangle); blend mode names map to composite operations (color dodge ↔ color-dodge, linear dodge ↔ lighter). Writing stores every layer at 0/0 plus the composite and a thumbnail.
  • Clipboard: navigator.clipboard.write/read with PNG where available, paste events with image files, and an internal clipboard as fallback.

Tests: tests/apps/test_imageeditor.py creates images with Pillow and checks pixels of the composite and the saved files: brush, pencil, undo/redo, picker, fill, shapes, selection, copy/paste, move, crop, layers with opacity and blend modes, OpenRaster round trip, PSD from psd-tools and back, flip, rotate, image and canvas size, adjustments with preview, filters, levels (preview, cancel, per channel, undo) and curves (point added by dragging, monotone result), magic wand with Shift/Alt, invert, intersect, lasso and polygon lasso, JPEG/WebP/BMP/PNG, GIF opening, text, gradient, zoom, German interface, phone layout. Firefox reports integer mouse coordinates, so the tests aim at integer page coordinates inside a pixel.

Diagram editor (apps/diagram)

ES modules: model.js (shapes, geometry, routing, text layout, history), drawio.js (file formats, uses fflate), main.js (UI).

  • Model: a document has pages with shapes (type, x, y, w, h, text, style) and edges (from/to = { id, ax?, ay? } for an attached end, fixed at a relative point when ax/ay are set, else floating; { x, y } for a free end; route; style). Floating ends meet the shape outline (polygon) on the line towards the other end; orthogonal edges leave at the side facing the other end and get one or two bends; curved edges are cubic Béziers along the exit directions. Arrow heads are drawn as paths (no markers), so exports look the same everywhere.
  • Shape libraries (model.js LIBRARIES, PRESETS): every library shape is an own type with an SVG path (shapePath) and a draw.io style (drawio.js TYPE_STYLE): core draw.io shapes where they exist (folder, component, doubleEllipse, swimlane, mxgraph.networks.* stencils), otherwise a core shape plus the key dgType (draw.io keeps unknown keys), e.g. the gateway as rhombus. Classes and entities are one cell with an HTML label (bold title, <hr>, lines; -- lines become further <hr>), as draw.io's own class shape. Crow's foot and hollow arrow heads map to ERmandOne… and block/diamond with endFill=0; hollow heads are filled with white so the line does not show through.
  • Rendering: Preact renders SVG; the same PageContent component renders into a detached element for the SVG export. Text is wrapped with canvas measureText and drawn as <tspan> lines (no foreignObject, which would taint the canvas of the PNG export).
  • Interaction: one pointer handler on the SVG with pointer capture (double-clicks are hit-tested with elementsFromPoint), drag modes for move, resize, band selection, connect and end re-attachment, grid snapping, two-finger pinch. Connection ports are drawn below the end handles of a selected edge (an attached end lies on a port).
  • draw.io: <mxfile> with one <diagram> per page; compressed diagrams (Base64, raw deflate, URI encoding) are read. Layer cells (children of the root) become page.layers (visible="0", locked=1); a shape or edge gets the id of its layer and of its outermost group ancestor (group, absolute geometry: child geometry is relative to the parent); locked=1 sets locked. Writing creates the layer cells and one group cell per group (bounding box of the members, members relative to it). The model functions layersOf, layerOf, isShown, isSelectable and inLayerOrder decide drawing order, visibility and what clicks, the selection frame and Ctrl+A may select; new objects get the active layer in changed(), pasted groups get new ids. UserObject labels, HTML labels (converted to text), edge label cells, exitX/entryX anchors and the usual shape styles are mapped. Style keys the editor does not use are stored in extra and written back. The clipboard holds an <mxGraphModel> like draw.io's. SVG exports carry the file in the content attribute, PNG exports in a tEXt chunk mxfile.
  • Excalidraw: rectangles, ellipses, diamonds, text (also inside containers), arrows/lines with bindings, images from files.
  • History: structuredClone snapshots of the document (100 steps), coalesced for quick property changes and nudging.
  • Automatic layout (js/layout.js): a small layered layout like Graphviz dot: cycles broken by reversing back edges (depth-first search), ranks by longest path, eight barycenter sweeps to reduce crossings, ranks as rows or columns with the nodes centred; unconnected shapes go in a row after the graph. Edges against the direction get side anchors so the orthogonal router leads them around.
  • Mermaid (js/mermaid.js): a line-based parser for flowcharts (node shapes, link types, labels, chains, &); unknown statements are skipped. Shapes are sized from their labels and placed with the layout; .mmd/.mermaid files open as diagrams.
  • Printing: printDiagram() puts the SVG export of every non-empty page into #dg-print (one sheet each, with a title); the print stylesheet shows only that container and scales each SVG to the sheet width; it is removed after afterprint.

Tests: tests/apps/test_diagram.py with draw.io files written by the test (compressed page, group, HTML label, exit anchor, unknown style key) and an Excalidraw file: drawing, connecting via ports, labels, saving (checked with ElementTree), pages, styles, undo/redo, align, distribute, type change, z-order, move with snapping, resize, nudge, delete with edges, copy/paste/duplicate, routing, arrows, detaching ends, SVG/PNG export and reopening, German interface, phone layout, printing (empty diagram, one sheet per page, print media), Mermaid parsing (shapes, links, labels, skipped statements), import with a left-to-right layout without overlaps, automatic layout with undo, .mmd files, unsupported diagram types.

Calendar (apps/calendar)

A classic-script application on top of shared/js/ical.js:

  • Times are zoned wall times ({ y, m, d, hh, mm, ss, date, tz }, tz = floating, UTC or a TZID). toInstant resolves TZIDs with Intl.DateTimeFormat (IANA ids, Windows names from a table, /mozilla.org/…/Region/City); unknown zones fall back to local time. Views work with instants in the browser's zone; editing keeps the event's zone. New events get the browser's IANA zone and a VTIMEZONE generated from this year's offset transitions (yearly RRULE with BYDAY=nXX).
  • Recurrence (expand): periods of the rule (day, week from WKST, month, year) produce candidate days (BYDAY with ordinals, BYMONTHDAY incl. negative days, BYMONTH, BYSETPOS); COUNT, UNTIL, EXDATE and overrides (RECURRENCE-ID) are applied. Wall times are compared numerically and only occurrences near the range are converted to instants, so long-running series stay fast.
  • Round trip: an event keeps its original component; when writing, the managed properties (UID, DTSTAMP, DTSTART/DTEND, SUMMARY, LOCATION, DESCRIPTION, RRULE, EXDATE, RECURRENCE-ID, CATEGORIES, STATUS, SEQUENCE, LAST-MODIFIED) are regenerated and all others (ATTENDEE, VALARM, X- properties) copied. VTODO/VJOURNAL and existing VTIMEZONEs are kept.
  • Editing a series: "only this" writes an override VEVENT (same UID, RECURRENCE-ID = original start of the occurrence) or an EXDATE; "all" changes the master (moving by the same offset as the edited occurrence). SEQUENCE is incremented.
  • Views: month grid, time grid with overlap layout (columns per cluster), agenda; pointer-based create/move/resize with 15-minute snapping, HTML5 drag & drop in the month view.
  • Free/busy (ical.js): an occurrence blocks time unless it is CANCELLED or TRANSP:TRANSPARENT; all-day occurrences only with an explicit TRANSP:OPAQUE (TRANSP is read but not managed, so it is written back with the component). STATUS:TENTATIVE gives BUSY-TENTATIVE. mergeBusy joins periods per type, freeSlots walks the days of the range inside the working hours (local time, optionally without weekends) and returns the gaps of at least the duration, freeBusyPeriods reads FREEBUSY values of VFREEBUSY components (start/end or start/duration, FBTYPE=FREE skipped) and freeBusyText writes a METHOD:PUBLISH calendar with one VFREEBUSY in UTC. The imported periods are cached per calendar component (WeakMap), so undo, which replaces the component, recomputes them.
  • Printing: printView() adds body.cal-printing and an @page rule (A4 landscape for month and week); the print stylesheet hides the shell, the side bar and dialogs, shows a heading and scales the time grid with zoom so that 24 hours fit one sheet.
  • Reminders: the first VALARM with a relative trigger (RELATED=START) is the event's reminder (minutes before the start); saving replaces only that alarm (-PnDTnHnM, ACTION:DISPLAY) and keeps the others. Every 30 s, checkReminders() looks at the occurrences of the next 8 days and shows the due ones once per session (Notification API when switched on and permitted, otherwise the shell banner).

Tests: tests/shared/test_ical.py compares the recurrence expansion with dateutil.rrule (ten rules across a DST change) and checks parsing, folding, time zones, VTIMEZONE, EXDATE/overrides and written events with icalendar. tests/apps/test_calendar.py runs the app in Europe/Vienna with a fixed clock: views, search, creating by dragging, editing one or all occurrences, deleting occurrences and series, moving and resizing, month drag & drop, all-day events, repeat rules from the dialog, visibility, import by UID, renaming, German interface, phone layout, reminders (read from VALARM, due once, written and removed), printing (page size, print stylesheet).

Database tool (apps/dbtool)

ES modules drivers.js and main.js; CodeMirror with @codemirror/lang-sql (dialect and schema for completion are reconfigured per session).

  • SQLite: sql.js (vendor/sql-wasm.js, global initSqlJs); the WASM binary is embedded (data-src, gzip + base64) and passed as wasmBinary, the CSP allows 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Statements run one by one with iterateStatements, so every statement has its own result or change count. Saving exports the database (db.export()).
  • Postgres: own client for protocol version 3 over a relay TCP connection: SSLRequest and startTls on the relay, startup message, cleartext, MD5 (own MD5 implementation; WebCrypto has none) and SCRAM-SHA-256 (PBKDF2/HMAC from WebCrypto, server signature checked), simple query protocol (RowDescription, DataRow, CommandComplete, ErrorResponse with all fields, NoticeResponse); queries are serialised. Numeric type OIDs are converted to numbers except int8/numeric (kept as text to avoid precision loss). The schema comes from information_schema (tables, views, columns, primary keys).
  • Editing: browsing selects the key columns (primary key, or rowid for SQLite) and hides them when they are not table columns; cell edits, inserts and deletes are single statements with a WHERE on the key.
  • Statement splitting for "run at cursor" respects quotes, identifiers, comments and Postgres dollar quoting.
  • Connections are stored through Suite.appdata (connection fields: name, host, port, database, username, password, ssl, insecure, url).
  • ER diagram (js/er.js): foreign keys from PRAGMA foreign_key_list (SQLite) or information_schema (Postgres, empty when the views are not readable); one draw.io vertex per table (label with the columns), one edge per foreign key, placed with the diagram editor's layered layout (apps/diagram/src/js/layout.js, shared through the import map); the XML is sent to the diagram editor with Suite.bridge.openIn.
  • History: statements run by the user (not browsing or explaining) are kept in localStorage (suite.dbtool.history, 200 entries, newest first, duplicates moved up, with database name, time and success). Explain prefixes the current statement with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (SQLite; rows id/parent/detail are turned into an indented tree) or EXPLAIN (Postgres).

Tests: tests/apps/test_dbtool.py — SQLite files from Python's sqlite3 (schema, several results, run at cursor, errors, create, browse, edit, insert, delete, rowid tables, CSV/JSON export, saving checked with sqlite3); Postgres through both relays against tests/helpers/pg_fake.py, a small protocol server on top of SQLite (SCRAM, MD5 and cleartext authentication, wrong password, SSL with the test CA, browsing and editing), saved connections in KeePass (checked with pykeepass and reopened) and JSON (without password), query history (failed entries, browsing excluded, reload, clearing), the SQLite query plan, and the ER diagram opened in the diagram editor (tables, view, key markers, relations, layering).

SSH client (apps/ssh)

xterm.js terminals (ES modules from vendor/esm/xterm, one Terminal with FitAddon per tab, created outside Preact and moved into the active tab's container) on top of the SSH engine (shared/js/ssh.js, Go x/crypto/ssh and pkg/sftp compiled to WebAssembly, transport = relay TCP connection). client.shell() requests a PTY (xterm-256color) and forwards terminal input (term.onData) and resizes; the touch key bar sends escape sequences and turns the next key into a control character. The SFTP panel uses client.sftp() (realpath, list, readFile, writeFile, mkdir, rename, remove, rmdir). Host keys: the engine calls the hostKey callback with type, SHA-256 fingerprint and key; the app compares it with the hostKey field of the saved connection and otherwise asks (accept once, accept and save, reject; a changed key shows a warning). Connections are stored with Suite.appdata (fields: name, host, port, username, auth, password, privateKey, passphrase, hostKey, url). Key pairs are generated by the engine (engine.generateKey(type, comment, passphrase): crypto/ed25519, ecdsa P-256 or rsa 4096, ssh.MarshalPrivateKey(WithPassphrase) in the OpenSSH format, MarshalAuthorizedKey, FingerprintSHA256; engine 0.2.0). Session logs collect the decoded shell output while recording and strip escape sequences when saved.

Tests: tests/apps/test_ssh_client.py against a local OpenSSH server (tests/helpers/ssh_fixtures.py, key authentication) through both relays: terminal input/output (read from the xterm buffer), session end and reconnect button, rejected host key, passphrase-protected key, SFTP listing/download/upload/mkdir/rename/delete/navigation, saved connection with host key in KeePass (checked with pykeepass), changed host key warning, German interface, phone layout with key bar, key generation (checked with ssh-keygen -y and -l, then authorized and used to log in), session log without escape codes, terminal output, known host keys listed and forgotten.

FTP/SFTP client (apps/ftp)

js/remote.js offers one interface (home, list, read/write with progress and an offset, size, setTime, mkdir, rmdir, remove, rename, close) for:

  • FTP — own client over relay connections: replies with multi-line handling, explicit FTPS (AUTH TLS + relay startTls), implicit FTPS (TLS connection), PBSZ 0/PROT P, TYPE I, FEAT/MLSD with fallback to LIST (Unix and Windows formats parsed), passive mode with EPSV and fallback to PASV. Data connections are separate relay connections to the control host (addresses in PASV replies are ignored, they are often private); with FTPS they are TLS connections. Uploads end by closing the data connection. Commands are serialised. Servers that require TLS session reuse on the data connection (e.g. vsftpd require_ssl_reuse=YES) are not supported, because the relay opens every TLS connection independently.
  • SFTP — the SSH engine (client.sftp()), host keys confirmed and saved with the site. Files are read and written in 1 MiB chunks (readAt/writeAt, engine 0.3.0), which gives progress and makes resuming possible; chtimes sets the modification time.

The local side uses showDirectoryPicker() (directory handles; recursive upload and download of folders); without it, files come from the file picker and downloads use Suite.files.download. Transfers run one after another from a queue with progress.

  • Resume: a failed read carries error.partial (FTP: the chunks of the data connection before the failure; SFTP: the chunks read). Download jobs keep it in job.partial and the next run reads from that offset (FTP REST n before RETR) and concatenates. Upload retries ask size() (FTP SIZE, SFTP stat) and send the rest (FTP APPE, SFTP writeAt at the offset). A smaller file with the same name on the other side offers resuming before a transfer starts.
  • Synchronize: localTree/remoteTree collect the files below both folders (at most 5000 each) as relative paths; compareEntry(local, remote, { mode, useTimes }) gives the status (same size = same unless times are compared, with 2 minutes slack for LIST minute precision) and the proposed action for the direction. Running it creates missing folders (local getDirectoryHandle(…, { create }), remote MKD) and queues normal jobs; uploads set the remote time to the local lastModified (MFMT / chtimes).

Tests: tests/apps/test_ftp.py against pyftpdlib (plain, explicit and implicit TLS with the test CA; each server gets its own IOLoop, lock and stop event because pyftpdlib shares them between instances) and the OpenSSH fixture: browsing, download, upload (300 kB), mkdir, rename, recursive delete, navigation, FTPS, wrong password, SFTP, LIST/MLSD parsing, local folder transfers via an OPFS stub (with an own relay that accepts the HTTP test origin), saved site, German interface, phone layout.

HTTP analyzer (apps/http)

ES modules model.js (request model, variables, body encoding, cURL, Postman v2.1) and main.js (UI, CodeMirror for request and response bodies).

  • Sending: build() resolves {{variables}} (environment before collection variables), adds Basic/Bearer authorization and encodes the body (raw with a content type per language, URL-encoded with + for spaces, multipart with an own boundary, file). Through the relay Suite.relay.http() is used (all headers in both directions, optional redirect following and untrusted certificates); directly, fetch with credentials: 'omit' (a failure is reported as a possible CORS block). The CSP allows connect-src http: https: for the direct mode.
  • Rows (params, headers, form fields, variables): the empty last row creates a row on the first input and keeps it on its table row element, so fast typing before the next render does not create two rows. Query parameters are derived from the URL and written back into it.
  • cURL: a shell-word parser (quotes, $'…', backslash line continuations) and the common options (-X, -H, -d/--data-*, --json, -F, -u, -G, -A, -e, -b); export groups each option with its value on one line.
  • Collections are Postman v2.1 JSON (folders, headers, raw/urlencoded/formdata bodies, basic/bearer auth, collection variables); environments are stored with Suite.appdata. The history (50 entries) is kept in memory only, because requests may contain secrets.
  • Scripts (scripts.js): each run creates a Worker from a data: URL that contains the pm runtime and the user's code as the body of an async function (no eval; the CSP gets worker-src data:). A data: worker has an opaque origin, so it cannot open the suite's IndexedDB or storage; it receives only the request, response and variables and returns test results, console output, changed variables and the changed request; it is terminated after 5 s (endless loops). Changed environment and collection variables are merged back; Postman event entries (prerequest, test) are imported and exported.
  • WebSocket: a URL with ws:/wss: (after variable resolution) switches the send button and the response area to a browser WebSocket (binaryType = 'arraybuffer', subprotocols from the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header, at most 2000 log entries).
  • OpenAPI (openapi.js, js-yaml from vendor/esm/yaml): local $refs are resolved with cycle protection; examples come from example/default/enum, allOf/oneOf and the type and format; the collection is saved as a Postman collection.

Tests: tests/apps/test_http.py against the echo server of the relay tests through both relays and directly: params/URL sync, headers, Basic auth, response headers, JSON/urlencoded/multipart bodies with environment variables, status classes, redirects, history, direct mode with and without CORS headers, cURL import and export, Postman round trip (with scripts), German interface, phone layout, pre-request script and tests (headers and variables from the script, passed and failed tests, console, variables written back, timeout, syntax error, sandbox without storage or DOM), WebSocket against tests/helpers/ws_echo.py (subprotocol, echo, server close code and reason, reconnect, client close), OpenAPI 3 YAML import (tags, server variables, path/query parameters, $ref schemas with a cycle, bearer and API-key security).

Python notebook (apps/notebook)

The app is built on the kernel of spike S-9 (shared/js/python-kernel.js, python-worker.js, Pyodide bundle from vendor/pyodide/bundle.json, see decisions D-025 to D-027): the worker is started from embedded text as a classic script, the Pyodide files are embedded with data-bundle. The kernel API gained removeFile.

  • Cells: every cell owns a CodeMirror view (Python or Markdown), created once and attached to the cell element by Preact. Outputs are kept in nbformat 4 form (streams merged like Jupyter) and rendered by an Output component; HTML, SVG and Markdown pass DOMPurify (no scripts, event handlers, external URLs).
  • Files: .ipynb read and written as nbformat 4.5 (cell ids kept or created); .py with # %% / # %% [markdown] markers (percent format) read and exported.
  • Console: a CodeMirror input with history on the same kernel; execution counts are shared with the notebook.
  • Keyboard: in a cell Shift/Ctrl/Alt+Enter; command mode (focus on the cell element) Enter, A, B, M, Y, arrows, Delete.
  • Restart terminates the worker and starts a new one; wheels installed in the session are installed again.
  • Export: toHtml() writes a standalone page (inline CSS) from the cells: Markdown and HTML/SVG outputs through the same DOMPurify filter as on screen, images as data: URLs, code escaped; PDF prints that page from a hidden srcdoc frame.
  • Variables: the worker's _variables() walks the cell namespace _ns (without modules, functions, classes and _ names) and returns name, type, shape/length, dtype and a repr cut to 200 characters as JSON; the app asks for it after every execution. _table(name) renders a DataFrame/Series (other objects through pandas.DataFrame(...)) with to_html(max_rows=500, max_cols=50), shown after DOMPurify.
  • Widgets: shared/js/python-widgets.py (embedded as #python-widgets, written to /tmp/suite/ipywidgets.py at start, so it is imported on demand) implements the ipywidgets 8 API without traitlets: every widget has a model id (<session>-<n>) and a state dict with the key names of the Jupyter models (_options_labels/index for selections, IPY_MODEL_<id> references for children, outputs for Output). The kernel sends {op: open|update|close, id, model, state} through _post_comm (worker message comm, onComm of Suite.python.start); _repr_mimebundle_ puts application/vnd.jupyter.widget-view+json into display outputs. apps/notebook/src/js/widgets.js keeps the models, draws the controls (Preact) and sends changes with kernel.widget(id, data) ({value}, {index}, {click}, {submit}, {selected_index}), one at a time, keeping only the latest pending value per widget, and showing it at once. _widget_event in the worker calls the widget's observers/callbacks; outputs go to the request and so to the cell that created the widget, unless an Output captures them: the kernel's _emit routes outputs (display, figures, results) to the innermost with out: and Output.__enter__ replaces sys.stdout/stderr. clear_output() outside an Output sends {output_type: "clear_output"}, which the page applies to the cell. interactive builds controls from abbreviations (tuples → sliders, lists/dicts → Dropdown, bool → Checkbox, str → Text, number v → slider from −v to 3v) and re-runs the function in its Output. Saving writes the state of the shown widgets (with children and nested outputs) to metadata.widgets in the Jupyter widget-state format; opening and restarting keep them as inactive models. A minimal IPython.display module is registered as well.

Tests: tests/apps/test_notebook.py (one page per browser): start without network requests, keyboard execution and command mode, Markdown rendering and sanitizing, console with history, file panel (upload, refresh after running, download, delete), wheel installation, opening and saving .ipynb (validated with nbformat), .py import and export, restart, German interface, phone layout, variable inspector (filtering, types, shapes, table viewer, updates after running), HTML export with and without code (sanitized Markdown, escaped code, outputs) and printing, widgets (slider with observe and Output, interact with Dropdown, buttons printing into the cell and raising, Checkbox, Tab, matplotlib in interact, saved state shown inactive). The kernel itself is covered by tests/prototypes/test_s9_notebook.py.

Spreadsheet (apps/spreadsheet)

Univer Sheets 1.0 (vendor/esm/univer-sheets, decision D-019) in a container that is created outside Preact and attached to the layout, with the file conversion of spike S-6 (shared/js/univer-xlsx.js: ExcelJS for XLSX/XLSM, SheetJS for ODS/XLS/CSV).

Conditional formatting and data validation come from the presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-conditional-formatting and -data-validation (pinned to the core's 1.0.4). Univer keeps their rules in the workbook resources (SHEET_CONDITIONAL_FORMATTING_PLUGIN, SHEET_DATA_VALIDATION_PLUGIN: JSON { sheetId: [rules] }); univer-xlsx.js maps them to ExcelJS worksheet.conditionalFormattings / addConditionalFormatting (cellIs, containsText, expression, timePeriod, top10, aboveAverage, colorScale, dataBar; differential styles ↔ Univer bg/cl/bl/it/ul/st) and to cell dataValidations. ExcelJS lists validations per cell; equal settings are joined into column runs again. Error styles: Univer INFO=0, STOP=1, WARNING=2. ExcelJS writes containsText rules without the text attribute, so reading takes the text from the formula.

  • Styles: the app loads vendor/pico.conditional.min.css, which styles only elements inside .pico; the shell's header, banner, toasts and dialogs carry that class, the Univer UI keeps its own look. Dialogs with .pico get a z-index above embedded editors.
  • Dirty state: CommandExecuted events of type mutation count as edits only within 3 seconds after user input (pointer, key, paste, cut, drop) in the editor container, and only if that input came after the latest load: Univer emits set-up mutations asynchronously after a unit is created. The document editor uses the same rule.
  • Theme and language follow the shell: univerAPI.toggleDarkMode() and univerAPI.setLocale().
  • Saving keeps the opened format (XLSM is saved as XLSX); CSV and XLS show a note that formatting is lost.
  • CSV import (js/csv.js, SSCSV): decoding (BOM, strict UTF-8, else Windows-1252), separator sniffing (the candidate with the most consistent column count over 20 rows), an RFC 4180 parser (line breaks inside quotes become \n) and value conversion; the rows go through Suite.univerXlsx.importRows() (SheetJS aoa_to_sheet → XLSX → ExcelJS → Univer). Dates are written as serial numbers computed in UTC with a yyyy-mm-dd format, because SheetJS would convert Date objects in the local zone. CSV export passes the import's separator to SheetJS (FS).

Tests: tests/apps/test_spreadsheet.py — opening, typing with recalculation, dirty marker, saving XLSX (checked with openpyxl), ODS, CSV, XLS, XLSM, discarding changes, language and theme, phone layout, CSV import dialog (Windows-1252, semicolons, decimal comma, quoted line breaks, leading zeros, dates, all-text mode, saving with the same separator). Import/export fidelity: tests/prototypes/test_s6_office_io.py.

Document editor (apps/document)

Univer Docs 1.0 with the docs core and docs drawing presets (vendor/esm/univer-docs, decision D-020), in the same structure as the spreadsheet (container outside Preact, conditional Pico, dirty rule, theme and language). DOCX import uses the direct reader of spike S-8 (shared/js/docx-import.js, through importDocx of shared/js/univer-docx.js), export uses the docx library (exportDocx). DOCM and DOTX are opened and saved as new DOCX files. ODT (shared/js/odt.js, own code on fflate): the reader resolves automatic and common styles with their parent chains (text and paragraph properties, lengths in cm/mm/in/pt), text:h outline levels, Title/Subtitle, lists with the text:list-style level kinds, tables (covered cells: horizontal spans are dropped, vertical ones become rowSpan: 0), frames with images, links, text:s/text:tab, notes (appended at the end) and the first master page (page layout, header, footer); it builds the Univer body with the Body builder of docx-import.js. The writer walks the Univer body like exportDocx and writes content.xml with automatic styles shared by equal properties, nested text:lists, tables with covered cells, Pictures/, plus styles.xml (headings, page layout, header and footer), meta.xml and the manifest, with mimetype stored first. Table of contents (shared/js/doc-toc.js): ordinary paragraphs whose text is a hyperlink to #toc-<n> (n = position among the headings, namedStyleType 4–8); insertToc cuts an existing table (found by these links) or uses the cursor paragraph (DocSelectionManagerService.getActiveTextRange()), pastes the new paragraphs and shifts all indices of the body; the document is reloaded as a new unit. The DOCX export wraps headings in Bookmarks and the entries in InternalHyperlinks, the ODT export writes text:bookmark and #toc-n links. The DOCX reader turns footnoteReference/endnoteReference into superscript labels and appends the note bodies at the end (as the ODT reader does). Plain text: lines become paragraphs (fromText); saving as text writes the data stream with paragraph marks as line breaks and without embedded objects (toText). Printing and HTML (shared/js/doc-html.js, toHtml): the Univer data becomes a self-contained page (named styles → h1–h5/title/subtitle, paragraph and run styles as inline CSS, links, nested ul/ol from bullet.nestingLevel, tables with colgroup widths, spans and shading, drawings as img, page breaks as break-before:page, headings with id="toc-<n>" for the table of contents links); @page takes the page size and margins of documentStyle, and with print the default header and footer are position: fixed in the margin boxes so they repeat on every page. The 🖨 button (Ctrl+P) loads it into a hidden srcdoc frame and calls its print() (CSP frame-src 'self' about:); saving as .html writes the same page without print. Spelling panel (apps/document/src/js/spelling.js, F7) on the suite's spell checker (see Spell checking): spell.errors of the body's data stream, grouped by word with their offsets; the language, personal and ignored words are those of the header selector. Selecting and replacing use the facade (FDocument.setSelection, getTextRange(start, end).setText, from the last occurrence backwards); the offsets are computed again before each action, as the text may have changed since the check.

Tests: tests/apps/test_document.py — opening a DOCX, typing at the start, dirty marker, saving (checked with python-docx), typing in a new document and saving as text, opening text files, rich DOCX with header/footer, templates, language and theme, phone layout, ODT round trip, table of contents and footnotes, print rendering (header, lists, table spans, images, heading anchors; Firefox blocks the page in print() under Playwright, so there the frame is caught before it loads) and HTML export, spelling (suggestion replaces all occurrences, personal dictionary, .oxt in ISO-8859-1, ignore, kept after a reload, .aff+.dic pair). DOCX fidelity: tests/prototypes/test_s8_docx_reader.py and test_s6_univer_docs.py. In Firefox, umlauts typed by Playwright are duplicated by Univer Docs' input handling; the typing tests use ASCII text.

Presentation editor (apps/presentation)

Own editor on the deck model of spike S-7 (decision D-021): shared/js/pptx-import.js (PPTX reader with layout/master inheritance, fflate), shared/js/slide-render.js (DOM/SVG rendering, text as editable HTML), shared/js/pptx-export.js (PptxGenJS) and Moveable for move, resize and rotate (with snapping guides).

  • Transitions and animations (slide.transition = { type, dir, duration, advanceAfter }, slide.animations = [{ id, effect, start }]): the reader takes the first p:transition (PowerPoint 2010+ writes it in mc:AlternateContent with p14:dur; otherwise spd, advTm) and the entrance p:cTns of p:timing (presetClass entr, presetID 1/10/2/53 → appear/fade/fly/zoom, nodeType → click/with/after), mapping spTgt spid to the elements by the p:cNvPr ids read with them. PptxGenJS writes neither, so pptx-export.js unzips its output and inserts p:transition and a main sequence (p:timing, one click group per "on click") after p:clrMapOvr; the shape ids come from the p:cNvPr elements in the order the elements were added. The show groups the animations the same way: elements of later groups are hidden, a step plays the next group with the Web Animations API (opacity, translate, scale); transitions animate the new (and for push the old) slide view; advance after is a timer that any navigation restarts.

  • The stage and the thumbnails are rendered imperatively into containers outside Preact; the panels are Preact. Pico is loaded in its conditional build so that slide content (tables, text) is not restyled; toolbar, panel and dialogs carry .pico (in the media query the toolbar selector is nav.pr-toolbar, because .pico nav would win otherwise).

  • Text editing uses contenteditable on the rendered text box (or table cell) and reads the result back with readText; formatting while editing uses document.execCommand, otherwise the properties of all runs of the element are changed.
  • Undo/redo keep structuredClone snapshots of the deck (60 steps, quick changes of the same kind coalesced). The clipboard holds copies of elements inside the page.
  • Presenting renders one slide scaled into a full-screen overlay; keyboard, click and swipe navigation. Printing renders every slide into a print container with @page of the slide size.
  • Speaker notes (slide.notes) are read from the body placeholder of the slide's notesSlide part (pptx-import.js) and written with PptxGenJS addNotes. The presenter view opens an about:blank window (same origin), copies the page's <style> elements into it and renders the current slide there; the console in the main window shows the current and next slide, the notes, a timer and the clock. Key presses in either window go to the same handler.

Tests: tests/apps/test_presentation.py — opening a PPTX, editing position, size and text formatting in the panel, saving (checked with python-pptx), adding text, shapes, tables (cell editing) and images, slides (add, duplicate, reorder, delete), undo/redo, nudging, copy/paste, moving with the mouse, presenting, save as and templates, German interface, phone layout, speaker notes (imported with python-pptx, edited, saved) and the presenter view (console, audience window, keys in both windows, ending). Import/export fidelity: tests/prototypes/test_s7_slides.py.

Mail client (apps/mail)

Own protocol clients on top of the relay TCP connections (Suite.relay.connect, TLS or startTls):

  • js/imap.js: IMAP4rev1 client. Responses are cut into complete lines including literals ({n}), then tokenized (atoms with [...] sections, quoted strings, literals as bytes, NIL, lists). Commands are serialized through a promise chain; untagged responses belong to the running command, EXISTS/EXPUNGE of the selected folder are also reported to onUpdate. Login with AUTHENTICATE PLAIN (SASL-IR or continuation) or LOGIN; literals with LITERAL+ or synchronizing. Folder names in modified UTF-7; special-use flags with name guesses (German/English) as fallback. Moving uses MOVE or COPY + \Deleted + UID EXPUNGE (EXPUNGE without UIDPLUS).
  • js/smtp.js: submission with EHLO, STARTTLS, AUTH PLAIN/LOGIN, per-recipient refusals, dot-stuffing.
  • js/mime.js: message building (7-bit only: quoted-printable text, base64 attachments, RFC 2047 headers, RFC 2231 file names, folded headers, multipart/alternative, related for pasted images, mixed), address lists, mbox split/join, vCard 2.1/3.0/4.0 parsing (unknown properties kept) and vCard 3.0 writing. Parsing of messages with postal-mime (vendor/esm/mail).

Several accounts: sessions maps account ids to { account, imap, folders, unread, folder, selected }; state.account/imap/folders/unread are those of the active session (activate), switching keeps the other connections open and NOOPs all of them every minute. selected tracks the folder selected on each connection (selectIn selects only when needed). The combined inbox (source: 'unified') selects every inbox, fetches its newest 50 summaries and tags them with uid = "<account>:<uid>", acc and realUid; reading, flags and deleting group the uids by account (byAccount) and act on that connection; replies take the message's account (messageAccount) and append the sent copy and \Answered through its session. EXISTS of a background inbox updates its unread count, or reloads the combined list.

js/main.js: accounts are appdata connections (passwords only when chosen; smtpPassword is a protected KeePass field), contacts are in the app settings (settings.contacts). Lists fetch UID FLAGS INTERNALDATE RFC822.SIZE and selected header fields in pages of 50 (sequence ranges); messages are fetched with BODY.PEEK[], parsed, cached (40) and marked \Seen explicitly. HTML mail is sanitized with DOMPurify (forms, frames, base removed; remote src/url() removed and counted; cid: images replaced by data URLs) and shown in a srcdoc iframe with sandbox without allow-scripts; the iframe inherits the page CSP, so remote content cannot load either. Invitations are read with shared/js/ical.js; replies are iMIP METHOD:REPLY messages with the attendee's PARTSTAT. Sent messages are appended to the \Sent folder, drafts to \Drafts (with Bcc, flags \Draft \Seen); sending an edited draft expunges it. A NOOP every minute picks up new mail.

Conversation threads (js/threads.js): the summaries also fetch In-Reply-To and References; a message's parent is the last message of its reference chain that is loaded, otherwise (no references, subject with a reply prefix) the earliest message with the same base subject; cycles are broken. The list shows threads collapsed (newest activity first) and expands them on demand; keyboard navigation follows the displayed order.

Rules and templates are stored in the account record (rules: [{field, contains, action, folder}], templates: [{name, subject, text, html, mode}]), so they travel with the application data file. applyRules runs on the summaries of unread inbox messages when the inbox is opened and when IDLE/NOOP reports new mail; it remembers the processed folder/uid pairs for the session, groups the UIDs per action and issues one MOVE/STORE/expunge per group. The ⚙ button applies the rules to all loaded messages of the current folder.

Tests: tests/apps/test_mail.py with tests/helpers/mail_fake.py (threaded IMAP and SMTP servers: literals with and without LITERAL+, MOVE or not, implicit TLS and STARTTLS, AUTH PLAIN/LOGIN) — reading HTML/attachments from .eml, mbox and search, composing (checked with Python's email), contacts and vCard, invitations, MIME helpers, German/phone layout, and through the relay (Python and PowerShell): folders, unread counts, flags, search, move, delete, new mail, reply/forward/send with sent copy and \Answered, drafts, TLS/STARTTLS with COPY+EXPUNGE and invitation replies, wrong password, folder creation and drag and drop; conversation threads from an mbox (references, subject fallback, depth, flat list); rules (move on demand, flag on arrival) and templates.

Audio editor (apps/audioeditor)

The Web Audio API plus, for compressed export only, Mediabunny with its MP3 (LAME) and FLAC (libFLAC) WebAssembly encoder extensions (vendor/esm/audio, MPL-2.0, loaded with a dynamic import() when the export dialog opens). js/dsp.js works on { rate, channels: [Float32Array] } and always returns new arrays. It contains range editing (slice, remove, insert, replace, pad), effects (gain, normalize, fades with a ramp that may span several clips, reverse, invert, echo), generators, a mixer (gain in dB, equal-power pan, mute, solo), peaks for drawing (min/max per 256 samples), an own WAV decoder (PCM 8/16/24/32 bit, float 32/64, extensible, RF64) and encoder (16/24 bit PCM scaled like the decoder, so that unchanged PCM is written back bit-identically; 32 bit float). Resampling, speed changes and biquad filters render through an OfflineAudioContext. Other formats are decoded with decodeAudioData of an OfflineAudioContext at the project rate.

js/clips.js: a track is a list of clips { id, offset (samples), audio, name, beats?, cues? }. Clips are immutable; every operation returns a new list, so undo snapshots (50) only copy the track objects. Range operations ripple like Audacity: removeRange cuts the range out of the clips it touches and moves later clips left, insertGap/insertClips split at the position and move later clips right, sliceRange copies the clips of a range (clipboard, trim), mapRange processes the parts of the clips in a range with the same length (most effects), mergeRange mixes the range into one clip for effects that change the length (speed, tempo, reverse), flatten mixes a track (gaps are silence, overlapping clips add up). Beats are a constant-tempo grid { bpm, phase } relative to the clip, cues sample positions in the clip; splitting and ripple edits carry them along, speed/tempo scale them.

js/beats.js: an onset envelope by spectral flux (radix-2 FFT, Hann window, hop ≈ 11.6 ms, log magnitude, positive differences, local mean removed); the tempo from the envelope autocorrelation weighted with a log-normal curve around 120 BPM (parabolic peak interpolation); then a fine search of period (±3 %, 0.05 % steps) and phase (¼ frame) that maximises the interpolated envelope at the grid positions. Accuracy with click tracks: ±0.05 BPM, phase within 2 ms. Cues: the first sample above −40 dBFS and envelope peaks above mean + k·σ (k from the sensitivity), strongest first, with a minimum distance. timeStretch is WSOLA (40 ms Hann frames, 50 % overlap, ±10 ms search: coarse on the mono mix decimated by 4, then ±3 samples at full rate; all channels use the same frame positions), about 0.5 s per 30 s of 44.1 kHz audio.

js/main.js: waveforms are drawn into one canvas per track that is as wide as the visible lane; the visible range is cached in an offscreen canvas (key: view, size, track version, colours, picked clip) with clips, their title bars, beat lines and cues; selection, cursor, snap line and playhead are drawn over it, during playback once per frame. Peaks and AudioBuffers are cached per audio object in WeakMaps. Dragging a clip by its title bar moves it live (between tracks as well) and records one undo step on release. Snapping collects the edges, beats and cues of all other clips, the playhead and 0 into a sorted array and, for every edge, beat and cue of the dragged clip, finds the nearest target by binary search (threshold 8 px). Playback starts one AudioBufferSourceNode per audible clip into a gain and StereoPannerNode per track; levels change live. Recording uses getUserMedia and MediaRecorder and decodes the result into a new track. Menus are fixed-position panels (a dropdown inside the horizontally scrolling toolbar would be clipped).
