js/project.js: .audioproj files are ZIPs (fflate) with project.json (format: "suite-audio-project", version, rate, tracks with name/gain/pan/mute/solo and clips with name, offset in samples, beat grid, cues and the path of their audio) and audio/<n>.wav (32-bit float, stored without compression; clips sharing an audio object share the file). Opening resamples to the project rate and scales offsets, beat phases and cues accordingly. Project labels are stored as labels: [{start, end, text}] in seconds.

js/effects.js: compressor/limiter (peak follower over all channels with attack/release coefficients, gain computer in dB), equaliser and reverb as offline Web Audio graphs (BiquadFilterNode shelves/peak; ConvolverNode with a deterministic decaying noise impulse response), pitch shift = WSOLA time stretch by 1/r followed by resampling with playbackRate r, noise reduction = spectral gate (STFT 2048/512 with Hann windows, noise level per bin from the quietest 10 % of the frames that lie fully inside the range, gains smoothed over neighbouring bins and decaying over time, overlap-add with window normalisation).

Clip volume and fades (clips.envelopeAt): gain in dB and equal-power fade curves (sin over the fade length) per clip, applied in flatten() (saving, export, effects that mix) and during playback as a GainNode with setValueCurveAtTime from the playback position to the clip's end. Splitting keeps the fade-in on the left and the fade-out on the right part; the project file stores gain, fadeIn and fadeOut. Cross-fade sets the fades of overlapping neighbours to the overlap length.

Volume automation: track.envelope is a sorted list of { t, db } points (seconds, −40…+6 dB), linear in dB between the points and constant before the first and after the last. withEnvelope() applies it to the mix of the track (mixdown, export, "Mix down to one track"); playback puts one more GainNode per track behind the clip sources and feeds it the curve with setValueCurveAtTime (sampled every 10 ms, at most 8000 values). The points are drawn over the lane while ⤴ is active; dragging is clamped between the neighbours, a double-click removes a point. The project file stores envelope per track.

js/labels.js: Audacity label text (start\tend\ttext, one per line; lines starting with \ – frequency ranges – are skipped, a missing end makes a point label). The label strip is a canvas drawn with the ruler; overlapping labels alternate between two rows, hit-testing uses the same layout (labelBoxes()). Labels are part of the undo snapshots and of the snapping targets.

Spectrogram (beats.spectrogram()): Hann-windowed 1024-point FFTs of the mono mix with a hop that keeps at most 6000 frames per audio object, levels quantised to bytes (-100…0 dB) and cached in a WeakMap; drawClipSpectrum() maps each device pixel column to a frame and each row to a bin on a logarithmic frequency axis and writes an ImageData through a 256-entry colour table.

js/encode.js: available() asks Mediabunny's canEncodeAudio per format (the browser's encoders first; the LAME and libFLAC encoders are registered only where the browser has none). encode() feeds the mix in 2-second AudioSamples (f32-planar) into an AudioSampleSource of an Output (Mp3OutputFormat, FlacOutputFormat, OggOutputFormat with Opus, Mp4OutputFormat with AAC) with a BufferTarget. MP3 is encoded at the project rate (at most 48 kHz), Opus at 48 kHz, AAC at 44.1 or 48 kHz. The encoders run in workers created from Blob URLs; the CSP therefore allows worker-src blob: and 'wasm-unsafe-eval'.

Tests: tests/apps/test_audioeditor.py (WAV files generated and checked with wave/struct) — opening, deleting with undo/redo and bit-identical saving, mouse selection over tracks, copy/paste, resampled import, mute/pan and mixdown, all effects, generators, WAV export (24 bit stereo selection, 32 bit float), 24-bit decoding, playback with loop, recording (fake microphone from an oscillator), splitting, dragging clips with and without snapping and into another track, ripple delete, clip menu (move to, duplicate, remove), beat detection and beat-to-beat snapping of two click tracks, cue detection, tempo matching with re-detection, beat grid by numbers, MP3/FLAC (and Ogg Opus where available) export, German interface and phone layout with touch, labels (keyboard and double-click, selecting, undo, Audacity export/import, removing, project file), spectrogram (peak bin and level of a 1 kHz tone, brightest row of the drawn view), fade handle dragging with undo/redo, clip volume, cross-fading overlapping clips, playback with fades, fades in the project file, compressor, limiter, equaliser, reverb tail, pitch shift by an octave (zero crossings, length), noise reduction (>10 dB less noise, tone within 1.5 dB) and effects through the menu.

Barcodes (apps/barcode)

ZXing-C++ compiled to WebAssembly (zxing-wasm 3, MIT; ZXing-C++ Apache-2.0) reads and encodes all codes. tools/vendor_zxing.py stores the ES module of the "full" build (reader and writer), its shared chunk and zxing_full.wasm in vendor/zxing/; the WASM is embedded (data-src, gzip + base64) and passed as wasmBinary to prepareZXingModule, so zxing-wasm does not fetch it from its CDN.

  • Reading: readBarcodes(ImageData, { tryHarder, maxNumberOfSymbols: 16 }) on images drawn into a canvas (files, drops, pasted images) and on camera frames (getUserMedia, about five frames per second, at most 1280 px wide). Results are listed once per format and text; their positions are drawn on an overlay canvas.
  • js/content.js recognises contents (URL, WIFI:, vCard and MeCard, mailto:/MATMSG:, tel:, SMSTO:, geo:, otpauth://, VEVENT) and builds them for the generator (with the escaping of WIFI:/vCard). Links are only offered for http(s) and open with rel="noopener noreferrer".
  • Generating: writeBarcode(text, { format, options: 'ecLevel=…' }) returns the symbol as a bitmap (0 = dark, without quiet zone); js/render.js draws it as SVG (identical rows merged into one path) and on a canvas (PNG) with module size, quiet zone, colours and, for 1D codes, bar height and text. The result is read back with tryInvert as a check (EAN/UPC may add the check digit).

Tests: tests/apps/test_barcode.py – an image with a QR code (segno) and an EAN-13 (zxing-cpp) read together, duplicates, links, empty images, vCard to .vcf and into the generator, PNG/SVG read back with zxing-cpp, Wi-Fi escaping, error correction, EAN example and invalid content, Data Matrix/Aztec/PDF417/Code 128, light-on-dark colours, a fake camera (canvas stream), German interface and phone layout.

Video editor (apps/videoeditor)

Based on spike S-10: WebCodecs through Mediabunny (vendor/esm/video, MPL-2.0).

  • js/timeline.js: the project model as plain objects and pure functions (overwrite edits with clearRange, move, trim, split, ripple delete, snapping, fade factor) plus the drawing of a clip (fit "contain", offset, scale, opacity, fades, titles) that the preview and the export share. Transitions (transitionIn/transitionOut) use the fade progress to clip (wipes, circle) or transform (slides, zoom) the drawing; exits are mirrored; only 'fade' changes the opacity, the sound always fades. Picture settings: a CSS filter (brightness, contrast, saturate) on the 2D context (also on the export's OffscreenCanvas), the crop as the source rectangle of drawImage, rotation around the picture's centre, and motion(c, t) interpolating scale and offset over the clip (Ken Burns). Speed and reverse: a clip covers (out - in) / speed seconds of the timeline; sourceTime(c, t) maps timeline to source time (backwards from out when reverse), and subClip(c, a, b) is used by overwrite edits, trimming and splitting, so the source range of every part stays correct. The export asks CanvasSink.canvasesAtTimestamps for the mapped times (descending for reversed clips) and plays the clip's audio as one buffer (reversed in place) with playbackRate = speed; the preview sets playbackRate (without preservesPitch) and seeks reversed clips frame by frame, muted.
  • Subtitles (js/subtitles.js): SRT/WebVTT cues (timestamps with , or ., optional hours, tags removed) become text clips on a video track named Subtitles; toSrt writes the text clips back with numbered cues. Undo keeps the previous project objects (100).
  • Preview (js/main.js): one <video>/<audio> element per clip (not in the DOM); syncMedia seeks or plays them to the timeline time (drift correction 0.3 s while playing), compose draws the active clips of the visible video tracks from bottom to top on the preview canvas. While paused, frames are drawn after seeked. Volume in the preview is capped at 100 % (media element limit); the export applies the real gain.
  • Export (js/export.js): availableFormats asks canEncodeVideo/canEncodeAudio; render composes every frame on an OffscreenCanvas (CanvasSource) with one sequential CanvasSink.canvasesAtTimestamps iterator per video clip; images are ImageBitmaps. The audio of all audible clips is decoded with AudioBufferSink, placed in an OfflineAudioContext (48 kHz stereo, gain automation for volume and fades) and added as one AudioBufferSource. Cancelling aborts and calls output.cancel().
  • Media are probed with Mediabunny (duration, size, canDecode, thumbnail); files it cannot read fall back to media element metadata (preview only). Project files are JSON (app: "videoeditor") with the timeline and source metadata; media are relinked by file name (import or "Locate…").
  • Waveforms: after loading a source with sound, loadPeaks decodes it once with OfflineAudioContext.decodeAudioData (files up to 400 MB) into 50 peak values per second; every audio/video clip draws its part (in…out, times the clip volume) into a canvas whose content is only redrawn when the clip, the zoom or the size changes.

Tests: tests/apps/test_videoeditor.py with media from tests/helpers/media_samples.py (ffmpeg of imageio-ffmpeg): import and probing, timeline layout, preview pixels, split/ripple delete/undo, dragging between tracks, trimming, properties, titles, export checked with ffmpeg (codecs, size, duration, pixels at given times), project save/open/relink, playback and frame steps, German interface and phone layout, waveforms (height of a tone, scaling with the volume, video clips), transitions (pixels in the middle of a dissolve, wipe, slide and circle), picture settings (brightness, rotation, crop, reset, motion at start and end; brightness in an exported file), subtitles (SRT and WebVTT import, burnt-in text, SRT export).

Web inspector (apps/webinspector)

Reduced browser wrapper (decision D-004), no libraries.

  • Pages are loaded with Suite.relay.http (all headers, no CORS) or, without a relay, with fetch (the CSP allows connect-src http: https: for this). Bodies are decoded with the charset of Content-Type or the <meta charset>. Every request is recorded (method, headers, status, body, time) and can be exported as HAR 1.2 (analyze.js toHar).
  • js/analyze.js: securityChecks (header rules with i18n keys), structure (DOMParser: meta, headings, links, images, scripts, styles, forms, frames and accessibility/security hints), HAR helpers (parseHar, mimeGroup, bodyOf, curl), previewDocument and highlightHtml.
  • The preview removes scripts, noscript, frames, objects, base, meta http-equiv, event handler attributes and javascript: URLs, makes links absolute and removes form actions. Through the relay it inlines stylesheets (and the url()s inside them), images, posters and inline-style images as data URLs (at most 80 requests). It is shown in a srcdoc iframe with sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-popups …" (no allow-scripts); the iframe inherits the page CSP, so nothing loads from the network. A click handler on the iframe document loads clicked links in the inspector. Resources that could not be loaded or are blocked lose their address (data-original-src, CSS url(data:,)), so the preview requests nothing. Preview sizes set the iframe's content box to the device size (box-sizing: content-box), so innerWidth and media queries match.
  • Cookies (analyze.js): parseSetCookie (RFC 6265 simplified: Domain must match the host, Max-Age wins over Expires, default path from the request path), storeCookies (replace by name/domain/path, expired cookies delete), cookieMatches and cookieHeader (longer paths first). With Keep cookies the jar lives in the page state and request() adds the Cookie header to relay requests. blockedBy(rules, url) matches host rules by suffix and * patterns against the whole URL (or without the scheme); blocked resources are recorded as requests with status 0. Preview size, rotation, rules and the keep-cookies switch are per-browser preferences in localStorage.
  • js/bookmarklet.js is embedded as text (<script type="text/plain">); bookmarkletUrl() removes comments, collapses whitespace and URL-encodes it (the file avoids line comments and relies on semicolons). The panel lives in a shadow root, hooks console.*, error and unhandledrejection, evaluates input with indirect eval, and reads Resource Timing, cookies and storage. Running it again toggles the panel (window.__suiteInspector).

Tests: tests/apps/test_webinspector.py with a local test site — loading through the relay (Python and PowerShell) with inlined styles/images, security checks, structure hints, source search, requests and HAR export, navigation in the preview and back; direct loading with CORS and pasted sources without relay; the HAR viewer (filters, sorting, JSON/image bodies, query/post data, timings, cURL); the bookmarklet on an HTTP page (console capture, evaluation, info, network, element picker, toggle) and in the app; German interface and phone layout.

Overview (apps/overview)

Contains all built apps: bundle.json lists dist/<app>.html, which build.py embeds gzip + base64 (the overview is therefore built last). An app is decoded on first use (DecompressionStream) and started by writing its HTML into an empty frame or window (document.open/write/close on about:blank). Such a document has the origin of the overview, so it keeps a secure context with File System Access API, Web Crypto and storage. Documents from Blob URLs do not on file:// in Chromium (opaque, insecure origin), and cannot be navigated to from other windows ("Not allowed to load local resource"). Written documents inherit the overview's Content-Security-Policy in addition to their own, so the overview's policy is the union of all app policies (checked by tests/apps/test_overview.py).

Frames and windows get the name suite-hub-app; Suite.bridge.hub() returns the parent frame or opener then. The overview relays “Open with…” requests into new tabs (no pop-ups) and receives dirty messages from Suite.shell.setDirty for the tab markers. “Save all apps” writes into a folder (showDirectoryPicker) or builds a ZIP (js/zip.js, stored entries). The overview is about 90 MB; it loads in about 2 s because the apps are only decoded when started.

Web slides (apps/reveal)

Diagram blocks (js/mermaid-svg.js) import mermaid.js, layout.js and model.js of the diagram editor through the import map (@diagram/…): the flowchart is parsed, laid out and drawn as an SVG string (shape paths, edges with arrow heads, labels with a background rect) in currentColor; the block keeps source, svg and error, and renderBlock only inserts the SVG. Drag and drop in the slide list uses HTML5 drag events (application/x-rv-slide); dropSlide takes the slide out (a main slide with its sub-slides) and inserts it before the target or as the target's last sub-slides. Print with notes passes showNotes: 'separate-page' to the print view.

Conversion with PowerPoint (shared/js/deck-convert.js, used here and in the presentation editor, which imports deck.js of this app for fromHtml/fromMarkdown): pptxToWebSlides orders the unlocked elements by position (rows within 20 px, then x) and maps title placeholders to headings, bullet/body placeholders to lists (levels as indentation), other text to text blocks (runs as <strong>, <em>, … and coloured spans except greys), pictures and tables; entrance animations become fragments (fragmentIndex = click group), transitions reveal.js transitions. webSlidesToPptx flattens the stacks and lays the blocks out from the top (HTML and Markdown slides are first turned into blocks with DOMParser / a small Markdown subset), estimates heights from font size and text length and scales everything down when it is taller than the slide; fragments (also on list items) become entrance animations, slides with dark backgrounds get white text.

Visual editor for reveal.js presentations. ES modules deck.js (model, HTML generation, import) and main.js (UI). The reveal.js builds, plugins, stylesheets, themes and fonts are embedded as text (<script type="text/plain">, see vendor/README.md), because the app writes them into the presentations it creates.

  • Model: deck = { title, lang, theme, highlightTheme, css, config, slides: [stack] }; a stack is a main slide with children (vertical sub-slides). A slide has kind blocks (heading, text, list, image, code, quote, table, HTML blocks with fragment effect and index, auto-animate data-id, alignment, size, colour), markdown (rendered by the markdown plugin: <section data-markdown><textarea data-template>) or html, plus background, transition, auto-animate, visibility, layout, auto-slide and notes (<aside class="notes">).
  • Output: renderPage(deck, assets) writes one self-contained HTML page: reveal.css, the theme's fonts, theme, highlight theme and custom CSS, the slides, the editor model as <script type="application/json" id="suite-reveal-deck">, reveal.js and the plugins inline, and Reveal.initialize with the deck configuration. Saved presentations therefore play offline and open again losslessly.
  • Preview: the same page with editable: true (blocks carry data-block) in an <iframe srcdoc> (same origin, inherits the app's CSP), configured embedded, without fragments, transitions and auto-slide. The editor attaches to the frame's document: clicks select blocks, double-clicks make them contentEditable (keyboard navigation of reveal.js is switched off meanwhile), formatting uses document.execCommand in the frame, and edited content is read back into the model without rebuilding the frame. Other changes rebuild the frame (debounced) and return to the current slide.
  • Presenting: a full-screen overlay frame, or a new window written via about:blank (speaker notes window and print view work there); the print view uses view: 'print'.
  • Import: own HTML (embedded model), other reveal.js HTML (sections become HTML slides; backgrounds, transitions, notes, theme link and common Reveal.initialize options are recognised), Markdown with ---/--/Note: separators, and Jupyter notebooks with metadata.slideshow.slide_type (slide, subslide, fragment, skip, notes), like nbconvert --to slides. Export also to Markdown.
  • Undo: Suite.UndoHistory with deck snapshots; typing in one field or one edited text is merged into one step.

The notebook keeps cell metadata, shows a slide-type selector per cell (“Slideshow”) and opens the notebook in the web slides app through the app bridge (“Slides”).

Formulas (D-042): usesMath(deck) looks for $$…$$, \(…\) and \[…\]; only then renderPage embeds KaTeX (vendor/katex: katex.min.js, auto-render.min.js and katex.css with the WOFF2 fonts as data: URLs) and calls renderMathInElement when reveal.js is ready (body[data-math=rendered]). reveal.js' own math plugin is not used because it loads KaTeX from a CDN. Markdown slides pass through marked, which would remove backslashes before punctuation and turn _/* into emphasis: mathForMarked escapes them inside formulas when the page is generated and mathFromMarked reverses this when a foreign presentation is imported. In the editing preview each block keeps its source (el.suiteSource), which startEditing restores, so texts are edited as TeX.

Tests: tests/apps/test_reveal.py edits texts in the preview, adds slides and elements, sets backgrounds, transitions, fragments, notes and deck options, checks the saved HTML and plays it offline in a new page (Reveal.getTotalSlides, highlighting), reopens it, imports Markdown, a notebook and a foreign reveal.js file, presents, and opens a notebook from the notebook app; plus slide structure with undo, German interface and phone layout; formulas (display and inline in Markdown, $ left alone, editing the TeX source, escaping in the saved file and on import, offline typesetting, no KaTeX without formulas).

Relay

The relay forwards TCP connections (WebSocket, with STARTTLS) and HTTP requests (without CORS restrictions). Implementations: relay/python/relay.py (standard library) and relay/powershell/relay.ps1 (no modules, no administrator rights). The protocol (version 2), the options and reverse proxy examples are in relay/README.md.

Protocol version 2 adds remote use: listening on other addresses (--bind) with an own TLS certificate or behind a reverse proxy (--trusted-proxy, --base-path, --host), user accounts (--users, PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes, created with --add-user, per-account target allow-lists), sessions (POST /auth, sliding expiry), rate limiting of failed logins, and sign-in by the reverse proxy (--proxy-user-header). Credentials are only accepted over TLS or from the local machine. Both implementations share the users file format and pass tests/relay/test_auth.py. The PowerShell relay keeps sessions and login failures in synchronized hashtables shared by its connection runspaces, and reads the browser side of a tunnel asynchronously, so that it also works over an SslStream.

shared/js/relay.js takes { url, token, user, password, allowInsecure } (Suite.relay.config): with a user name it logs in, caches the session per relay and credentials, and logs in again once when the relay answers invalid token or session expired. It refuses to send credentials to http:// addresses of other machines unless allowInsecure is set. The relay settings form (appdata.js RelayFields) offers the sign-ins token, user name and password, and reverse proxy / client certificate; data.relayConfigured() tells the apps whether the settings are complete. The apps that use the relay allow connect-src http: https: ws: wss: so that the relay can run on any host.

Tests

bash

The tests open the built HTML files from file:// in Chromium and Firefox. They check that pages make no network requests and produce no console errors. Shared modules are tested through the testbed testbeds/shared; file access with the File System Access API uses picker stubs backed by the origin private file system (served over http). Interoperability is checked with pykeepass, openpyxl, python-docx, python-pptx, nbformat, LibreOffice and an OpenSSH server.

pytest --mobile runs every browser test on a phone display (393 × 851 CSS pixels, device scale 2.75, touch; Chromium also emulates a mobile browser with is_mobile): the browser fixture wraps new_context so that every context gets these options unless a test sets its own viewport (tests/helpers/devices.py). The tests then act like a phone user: before an action (or expect(...).to_be_visible()) on an element that exists but is hidden, the navigation buttons (☰/Panels, Slides, ‹ Groups, ‹ Entries, ←, Media/Properties tabs) are tapped until it is visible; before an action on an element covered by an open drawer or its shade, and before raw mouse input on a point the drawer covers, the drawer is closed by tapping the shade. Elements that no visible button reveals still fail. Run the suite once normally and once with --mobile.

SUITE_DIST=<directory> makes build.py write the apps to another directory (the overview embeds the apps from there as well) and the tests open them from there, so that changes can be built and tested while another test run uses dist/.

Recovery copies (autosave)

shared/js/autosave.js: apps call Suite.autosave.register({ app, save, restore }); save() returns a structured-cloneable snapshot (or null), stored in IndexedDB suite-autosave (one record per app, works on file:// in Chromium and Firefox; file handles and Blobs are kept). Suite.shell.setDirty(true) schedules a copy (interval 15 s, localStorage['suite.autosave.interval'] in tests) and visibilitychange to hidden stores at once; setDirty(false) deletes it unless a found copy still waits for the user's decision. On start a banner (Suite.shell.banner(message, actions)) offers Restore/Discard; restoring stores a fresh copy and sets the app dirty. Snapshots above 64 MB are skipped. Per app: text editor (changed documents with handles and saved text), hex editor (bytes), diagram (draw.io XML), image editor (OpenRaster), spreadsheet and document (Univer snapshots), presentation and web slides (deck objects), notebook (ipynb), audio editor (project file), video editor (project and media up to 48 MB), calendar (iCalendar texts of changed calendars), database tool (SQLite exports of changed databases), HTTP analyzer (Postman collection), archive (the archive written with level 1, without passwords), PDF viewer (bytes with form data, annotations and page changes); not KeePass. Test: tests/apps/test_autosave.py (each app: change, copy, second tab restores, discard).

Keyboard shortcut overview

The section "## Keyboard shortcuts" (German: "## Tastenkürzel") of docs/<lang>/apps/<app>.md is the single source of an app's shortcut list: tables |Ctrl+S| Save | (alternatives a / b), grouped by ### Group headings. build.py replaces <script type="application/json" data-shortcuts="<app>"> with #suite-shortcuts ({"en": [{group, keys, text}], "de": [...]}); the build fails if an app has none. The shell lists them in the ? dialog for the current language and opens it with F1 (and ? outside of text fields). Test: tests/apps/test_shortcuts.py (every app, both languages, the number of rows matches the documentation).

Command palette

The end of shared/js/shell.js holds Suite.palette: when opened it collects the enabled buttons, tabs, a[href="#"] links and the options of select menus inside #app (not in dialogs, not the shell's theme/language/about/⌘ buttons), labelled by title/aria-label and text, de-duplicated; Suite.palette.register(provider) adds app-defined entries. Running an entry clicks the element (or sets the select's value and fires input/change) after the palette has closed and the focus is back, so apps see an ordinary user action. Search folds case and accents; all words must match. Keys: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Space (capture phase; Firefox reserves the first). Test: tests/apps/test_palette.py (every app has entries without the shell buttons; running a menu entry and a button; app-registered entries; calendar and hex editor).

Accessibility

shared/js/shell.js gives icon-only buttons (button, [role=button], a, summary with a title and no two-letter word in their text) their title as aria-label, through a MutationObserver on the whole document (also titles that change with the language); labels set by an app are kept (the automatic ones are marked with data-auto-label). shared/css/suite.css defines --suite-selected (light and dark) for selected rows and list entries – Pico's --pico-primary-focus is too dark for links and coloured text on it (WCAG 4.5:1) – and a :focus-visible outline for every element. The command palette is a combobox with aria-activedescendant; tab bars use role=tablist/tab with aria-selected as strings (Preact drops false); CodeMirror editors get an aria-label through EditorView.contentAttributes. Test: tests/apps/test_accessibility.py runs axe-core (axe-playwright-python, WCAG 2.1 A/AA rules) on the start screen of every app in light and dark mode and on the shell dialogs (shortcut overview, palette); the Univer surfaces and CodeMirror's syntax colours are excluded.

Recent files and window title

Suite.files.remember(app, handle) keeps up to ten FileSystemFileHandles per app in IndexedDB (suite-recent-files) and fires a suite-recent event; Suite.files.forget(app) clears them. Suite.shell.Recent (<${Suite.shell.Recent} app=… onOpen=… before=… />) is the shared select: it reloads on the event, asks before() (unsaved changes), calls Suite.files.reopen (permission prompt) and onOpen({ file, handle }). It renders nothing without the File System Access API. Suite.shell.setFileName(name) sets the window title to "name – app". Test: tests/apps/test_recent_files.py (eleven editors, picker stubs on the origin private file system).

Phone layout

Below 760 px the shell stylesheet turns the header toolbar (.suite-header > nav) into a full-width, horizontally scrolling row below the title. Side panels carry the class suite-drawer (fixed position, from --suite-top to the bottom, 20 rem wide at most) and are shown by the app's own open class. shell.js keeps --suite-top at the bottom edge of the header and banner (ResizeObserver), because the header wraps to two or three lines on phones; drawers must never cover it, so the button that opened a drawer can always close it. Apps render Suite.shell.backdrop(onClose) next to an open drawer: a shade below the drawer (hidden on wide screens) that closes it on a tap. Toasts ignore the pointer, so they never block buttons.

Documentation

The documentation is written in Markdown in docs/en/ and docs/de/. tools/build_docs.py converts it to Confluence storage format in docs/confluence/ (code blocks become code macros, notes become info/warning macros, links between the documents become page links). tools/build_docs.py --check fails if the generated files are out of date.
